open_points.subject: backup SQLite snapshot ownership and dependency
open_points.text: and any file — the store's file is `store`'s, a file in the backup location `backups`' (above). It is part of the store of A17 and A18: only `store` calls it, inside the transaction `store` opened, so no other module touches the database through it.
open_points.question: Which module opens, sanitises and integrity-checks the SQLite copy used by A18, and what is the permitted dependency direction between `backups`, `store` and `store_persistence`?
options: `backups` owns the files but calls a `store` operation that creates, removes AgentSession rows from and checks the copy
`store` produces a sanitised checked snapshot which `backups` only encrypts and manages
`backups` opens the copy and calls `store_persistence`, as an explicit exception to the rule that only `store` calls it
`backups` independently implements the SQLite removal and checks
open_points.default_guess: `backups` owns backup-file orchestration and calls a `store` snapshot/check operation; `backups` never imports `store_persistence` directly.

witness.initial: The live store contains an AgentSession and a daily backup is due.
events: The backup scheduler asks `backups` to make a backup.
`backups` creates a SQLite copy in the backup location.
The copy must have its AgentSession rows removed and must pass SQLite integrity and sequence checks before encryption.
outcomes: `backups` calls `store`, so `backups` depends on `store` and `store` operates on a file owned by `backups`.
`backups` opens or modifies the SQLite copy itself, so it depends on SQLite schema knowledge or `store_persistence` despite the statement that only `store` calls it.
witness.observer: The dependency projector and an owner restoring the backup see the difference.

open_points.subject: ownership scope of files outside the two named locations
open_points.text: and any file — the store's file is `store`'s, a file in the backup location `backups`' (above).
open_points.question: Does “any file” include the in-memory uploaded import file, the temporary store file, SQLite journal/WAL/SHM files and other engine files; if so, which module owns each one?
options: “file” means only filesystem files, with store temporary and SQLite sidecar files included in `store`'s ownership
“file” means every object called a file, so the upload must also be assigned to `store` or `backups`
The upload belongs to the import/owner-session module, store construction files belong to `store`, and backup-location files belong to `backups`
Engine-created sidecars belong to `store_persistence` even though the configured store file belongs to `store`
open_points.default_guess: Treat the clause as filesystem ownership: `store` owns the configured store, its construction temporary file and SQLite sidecars; `backups` owns every filesystem file in the backup location; the in-memory upload belongs to the import/owner-session module.

witness.initial: Registry has a live owner session, no uploaded import, and a configured store path.
events: The owner uploads an import file, which A16 keeps only in process memory.
A later start creates a new store under its temporary name and SQLite may create engine sidecar files.
outcomes: A broad reading of “any file” requires all of these to be owned by either `store` or `backups`, but the text supplies no classification for the upload or non-final store files.
A filesystem-only reading leaves the upload with the import/owner-session module and treats temporary and sidecar files as parts of `store`'s file.
witness.observer: The import, startup and persistence module implementers see different ownership and dependency boundaries.

open_points.subject: `store_persistence` model imports
open_points.rule: `module_internal[consumer][provider]` — **полный и минимальный** прямой runtime import surface consumer-модуля, а не копия публичного API provider-а: ровно те символы, которые код consumer-а называет напрямую — вызывает, конструирует, проверяет (членство в enum, тип), пишет в аннотации.
open_points.question: Replace the provider-wide `models` dependency with the complete minimal list of model, enum and interface symbols that `store_persistence` directly names in its repository, schema and row-codec runtime code.
